one_month_reasoning: No Lumentum earnings inside the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected around Nov 9-10, 2026, after Nov 1 [19]. The main events in the window are the hyperscaler September-quarter reports in late October (Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta around Oct 27-29, Amazon around Oct 29-30). Their 2027 capex commentary is the biggest read-through for optics. Consensus already has 2027 capex near $1T [15], so the bar is high. Optical peers mostly report in early November (Coherent), so they are also outside or at the edge of the window. The stock rose about 20% in four sessions, from about $908 on Sep 28 [16] to $1,085, at the 52-week high, in a sector-wide optics rally [17]. Short-term reversal after a sharp sector spike roughly offsets momentum, and sector selloffs on supply-chain headlines are frequent [16]. So I keep the distribution almost symmetric, with the median at about $1,080 (slightly below spot to allow for some giveback) and a monthly sigma of about 25%. That is near the brief's annual-vol/3.5 rule (97%/3.5 = 28%), trimmed a little because the realized 97% includes the parabolic re-rating.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS of about $38 x 30 = $1,140) and 40% cycle-normalized P/E (mid-cycle EPS of $27 x 28 = $756), giving about $985 per share on about 101M non-GAAP diluted shares.

bear.story: 2027 brings the LightCounting 'bumpy ride' [10]. Hyperscalers digest capacity after a ~$1T capex year [15], the laser shortage flips to surplus as Coherent, Broadcom, Sumitomo and Mitsubishi add capacity [4][11], and EML ASPs fall. Cloud Light module margins stay weak. EPS of about $25 at 20x.

base.story: The Q1 FY27 guide of $1.25B is met and growth continues through FY28. 1.6T EML content doubles [12][14], OCS and Nvidia CPO lasers layer in [1][18], and EPS run-rate is about $38. The multiple compresses from about 50x to about 30x, so the price ends roughly flat to slightly up.

bull.story: Supply stays tight through 2027 as 1.6T and then 3.2T roll out. CPO/ELS and scale-up optics start early [18], management's $40+ is beaten on the way to ~$45 NTM EPS, and the stock keeps a ~42x AI-infrastructure multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $600 is about 16x the ~$36-38 FY28 EPS. The stock would only trade there if the market had stopped believing FY28 estimates: for example, a hyperscaler capex cut for 2027, loss of Nvidia CPO/laser exclusivity, or a quick EML price collapse as industry capacity doubles. Ordinary volatility at a 97% realized vol could reach the $750-850 range without breaking the thesis.

reasoning: Company facts: Q4 FY26 revenue was $1.01B (+109% y/y), non-GAAP gross margin 50.4%, EPS $3.23. The Q1 FY27 guide is $1.25B and $4.20 EPS, and it hits the target model early [1]. Sell-side FY28 EPS is $30-39 [3] and management says about $40 [20]. At $1,085 the stock trades at about 50x NTM and about 29x FY28. Industry lane: the rest of the chain confirms demand through at least mid-2027. Coherent's FY27 order book is basically full, its InP output is up 80% and it sees no CPO delays [4][5]. Fabrinet data-center revenue is +68% [6]. Ciena guides FY27 +30% with a backlog above $10B [7]. InnoLight and Eoptolink grew H1 revenue +182% and +100% on 1.6T [8][9]. Hyperscaler capex is heading toward about $1T in 2027 [15]. EML content doubles per module from 800G to 1.6T, and Lumentum is the main 200G-per-lane EML source and Nvidia's CPO laser partner [12][14][18]. The chain also raises the main risk. EML/CW laser capacity doubled in 2026 [11], Coherent will double InP capacity again by end-2027 [4], and LightCounting expects the laser shortage to ease by end-2026. It also warns that growth runs come in 2-3-year bursts followed by flat or down years [10]. By Oct 2027 the market will price 2028-29, when pricing normalizes. Fair value comes from a forward P/E ($38 x 30 = $1,140) and a cycle-normalized P/E ($27 x 28 = $756), blended to about $985. That is close to spot, so I set the median a little below spot at about $1,050 and the scenario mean at about $1,210 (bear $500/25%, base $1,150/45%, bull $1,900/30%). Spread: a lognormal with sigma of about 0.70, below the 97% realized vol because the realized figure includes a one-off re-rating, with a slightly fatter left tail for a cycle turn. The base rate for a stock up 500%+ in a year with ~50x multiples is wide two-way outcomes, so I avoid strong directional confidence. Research was limited to about 16 searches and fetches; one Substack page returned 404 and only its search snippet was used.
